purpose: Establish whether Entu supports per-property sharing on ONE entity (branch i) vs requiring the two-entity fallback ruled in advance
method: throwaway _probe_ type with two prop-defs at different sharing tiers on one entity; verified via a genuinely non-privileged read (anonymous, no Authorization header) as a stand-in for a domain-tier caller with no specific grant on the instance — same code path (cleanupEntity tier selection), one tier further out; source-read confirms the mechanism is identical across domain/public

sourceEvidence.aggregateJs: utils/aggregate.js:112-120 resolves `sharing` PER PROPERTY DEFINITION inside the per-property loop (not per-type); only downgrades public->domain when the type itself is domain-capped (gate 2); a prop-def's own sharing value is otherwise untouched regardless of sibling prop-defs on the same type
sourceEvidence.cleanupEntityJs: utils/entity.js:569-612 selects private/domain/public bucket to serve based on the CALLER's own tier (owner-or-editor-or-viewer -> private; authenticated no-grant + entity.access includes domain -> domain bucket; access includes public -> public bucket); the domain/public buckets are the per-property-filtered objects aggregate.js built
sourceEvidence.accessArrayJs: utils/rights.js:76-97 getAccessArray: instance's own _sharing string plus every _viewer/_expander/_editor/_owner reference feed the access array cleanupEntity checks

liveSteps.result: GOTCHA: server auto-inherited _sharing=public from the parent TYPE (create-time inheritParentProperties), NOT private-by-default; corrected with an explicit DELETE-old-value then POST _sharing=private

liveSteps.step: CREATE one instance, _sharing=public, both fields populated

liveSteps.result: both fields present (expected, db-root sees the private bucket)
probe_public_field PRESENT with its value; probe_private_field COMPLETELY ABSENT from the response (not null, not empty — the key does not exist)

liveSteps.step: teardown: DELETE instance, both prop-defs, type (in that order)
liveSteps.result: all 200 {deleted:true}; re-GET of the type confirmed 404

conclusion: Per-property sharing on ONE entity is fully supported and empirically confirmed. A prop-def's own sharing tier is honored independently of sibling prop-defs on the same type, at both the aggregation (write) side and the tier-selection (read) side. Branch (i), single admin_member_record-shaped entity with name=domain / phone,email,birthdate=private, is the correct choice; the two-entity fallback is not needed.
correctionCarriedIntoTheShapeProposal: Every admin-only prop-def on a domain-shared type MUST explicitly declare _sharing:private at create time — omitting it does not default to private, it inherits the PARENT's (type's) own sharing, which would silently expose it
